indications: Wind disorders (All types of wind disorders).

1010.01.additionalInfo: There are three meetings (Hui) on the head: 1010.01 Zheng hui, 1010.05 Qian hui, and 1010.06 Hou hui. Together, they are called the three meetings of the head, Tou San Hui [ EN. These three points affect the brain and treat wind disorders but have different innervations and indications. They can be needled together using the Dao ma technique. The three meetings are important points for treating wind disorders, such as stroke, tics, epilepsy, tremors, and Parkinson's disease. They can be needled together or selected through palpation along the entire line. In Tung acupuncture, the points on the head (area 1010) are exceptional because Tung acupuncture treats the problem remotely rather than directly addressing it. This is a wise way to avoid direct interference. However, it is different in the case of the brain. Point Name Zhéng — upright, fair, straight, vertical, to correct. Hui [9] — meeting. One of the meanings of Zheng is to correct. The name of the point implies its ability to correct the Qi. This is the same character as Zheng qi (the correct Qi). Therefore, the name of the point suggests its ability to correct the meeting of Heaven (the head represents Heaven). It can reconnect us to Heaven. Heaven is also related to Yang Qi. The point can correct the Yang Qi. In extreme cases, an imbalance of Yang Qi generates wind. The point can also correct upright posture. The Yang Qi pulls the vertex upward.

1010.04.additionalInfo: The point has the same indications as 1010.02 Zhou Yuan, with the addition of a brain tumor, headache, and dizziness. When using the point for a brain tumor: prick the point on the right side for a brain tumor on the left side, and vice versa. The three points, 1010.02 Zhou Yuan, 1010.03 Zhou Kun, and 1010.04 Zhou Lun, have similar indications and innvert the lungs. These are important points for treating limb weakness - in Chinese medicine, Wei syndrome is based on lung weakness. Chapter 44 of the Su Wen on Wei syndrome states: "When the lungs are hot and the lobes are burning, the skin and hair are thinned and exhausted. The skin is taut and the hair is thin. When the heat is stuck, it causes laxity with inability to walk." The heat that sometimes originates from the heart (excess passion) harms the lungs, and the weak lungs do not circulate qi and blood into the limbs. As a result, atrophy of the limbs (Wei syndrome) was created. The Zhou points affect the brain and represent the metal (lung nerve), water (kidney nerve), and fire (heart nerve) phases. There are ten Zhou points: five are the kidneys, four are the lungs, and one is the heart. Strangely, there are no points related to wood (liver) because what usually causes damage to the brain is wind that rises up and can also turn into fire. In terms of Tung acupuncture, the wind of the wood is treated through the metal that controls the wood and brings down the excess of the wood. Therefore, in Tung acupuncture, the kidneys, heart, and lungs control the brain. Point Name Zhöu [1+11 - prefecture, (old) province, administrative division, state, oblast, canton. Lün [W] — Kun Lün mountain. Zhou is also a province. Each of the Zhou points is associated with a different Zang, a different province, and therefore affects the brain differently depending on the innervation of the associated organ. For example, 1010.25 Zhou Shui is associated with the kidneys (water), while 1010.23 Zhou Huo is associated with the heart (fire). Kun Lun If you connect the name 1010.03 Zhou Kun with 10101.04 Zhou Lun, you get the name Kun Lun, a mountain range originating in the Pamirs Plateau province, the westernmost region of China. The west is associated with metal (lungs), so the point's name suggests its effect on the lungs (lung innervation). In Chinese mythology, Mount Kun Lun is considered sacred. The Kun Lun Mountains appear in the Neijing Tu [ J, a Daoist diagram describing the internal channels of the circulation of qi in Neidan practice, first mentioned in the Qing Dynasty. The diagram depicts a side view of the body. In the head area, we find the Kun Lun mountains, like the Kun Lun points on the head.

1010.05.additionalInfo: The point has an immediate effect on a person who has lost consciousness. The point is used to wake up a patient from a coma. 1010.01 Zheng Hui, 1010.05 Qian Hui, and 1010.06 Hou Hui are often combined together in the Dao ma technique to affect the brain. For additonal information, see 1010.01 Zheng Hui. Hu Wen Zhi One of Tung's 32 relieving points that can treat a condition of brain toxicity, such as brain swelling, infections, or severe insomnia. Sleep is very important for brain health. A great lack of sleep can be seen as a state of brain toxicity, where the brain fails to rest and clean itself. Point Name Qiån [fifi] — front. Hui [f] — meeting. The front in the point's name implies that it is the most anterior of the three meeting points in the head and affects the brain's frontal region (the frontal lobe).

1010.07.additionalInfo: The point's primary use is vomiting, and it is also a main point for treating vomiting. The point treats wind affecting the brain, which can cause vomiting. Chapter 42 of the Su Wen states that when the brain is damaged, it can affect the stomach and intestines. In the Indications, Mater Tung mentions disorder in the six Fu organs, which means disorders in the stomach and intestines. Huo Luan Gill—Sudden turmoil disease is simultaneously characterized by diarrhea and vomiting, accompanied by abdominal cramps. Sometimes, it translates as cholera. Bleeding the point treats Sudden turmoil disease of the liver because the point can treat wind. The point innovates the Dan tian. There are three Dan tian in the body: the lower (kidneys), the middle (heart), and the upper (brain). The back region of the head is associated with water, so the point belongs to the lower Dan tian. The point is a pivot that brings the wind back down to the lower Dan Tian. Point Name Zöng [4] — to gather, collect, assemble. Shü — axis, pivot. The point's name suggests its location between the neck and the brain. This point is a pivot where wind can enter the brain. The wind entering the head causes a turmoil of Yang in the head, which can manifest as vomiting.

1010.08.additionalInfo: Due to the point's influence on the brain and heart, it establishes the connection between the kidneys and the heart. In Tung's acupuncture, the kidneys and heart influence the brain: the kidneys affect the brain tissue and nerves, while the heart influences consciousness and blood vessels. This is an important point that may calm the patient. I like to needle together in the Dao ma technique 1010.08 Zhen Jing with 1010.01 Zheng Hui and GV-22 Xin Hui to calm the patient. Point Name Zhén [SA] - Post, garrison, town, village. Jing [5+1 — Calm, quiet, stillness. The name of the point suggests its ability to calm.

1010.13.additionalInfo: The point can treat urinary system disorders caused by deficiencies in the kidneys and lungs. Nephrolithiasis (kidney stones) While acupuncture does not physically crush kidney stones, it is a highly effective treatment for facilitating their natural passage, provided the stones are smaller than 6 millimeters. Rather than breaking the stone, the treatment focuses on creating the optimal physiological conditions for its expulsion. It works by relaxing and dilating the smooth muscle of the ureters (spasmolysis), allowing the stone to pass without getting stuck. Additionally, acupuncture promotes diuresis, creating a natural hydraulic pressure that helps flush the system, while simultaneously reducing the local inflammation and tissue swelling that can narrow the urinary tract. Ultimately, this approach significantly relieves the severe pain of renal colic and supports the smooth, natural exit of the stone. Point Name — Horse. Jin — Gold, Metal. Mä — Horse. Jin — Gold, Metal. Shui [7k] — Water. Metal-water points strengthen the kidneys and lungs. The point's name hints at this ability. The term "fast horse" describes the point's quick and strong effect. Mä [X] — Horse.

1010.19.additionalInfo: 1010.19-20 Shui Tong/Jin are needled together using the Dao Ma technique, often bilaterally. For lower back pain, needle on the opposite side of the pain. These points treat kidney deficiency, which is one of their main indications. Another indication for using the points is the presence of green-blue hues, dark skin, wrinkles, or Luo channels in the point area. The two points together Harmonizing the kidneys and lungs enhances the descending of lung Qi and the anchoring of Qi by the kidneys. Hence, some sources use these points for breathing difficulties, bronchitis, asthma, and emphysema due to kidney deficiency. The points can be used for joint diseases due to kidney deficiency. They can also be used for kidney stones and an enlarged prostate. Master Tung's Cases For finger swelling, use 77.09 Si Hua Zhong first, and if the condition does not improve, add 1010.19-20 Tong Shui/Jin. Severe hiccups: 1010.20 Tong Jin bilaterally.
